messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging: P0 - 5xx spike and ELB target draining in us-west-2c. Affected: api.redwood.example.com. Alert group: api-frontend-5xx. Priority: High

maria: seeing ~40% 5xx in us-west-2c, error is ELB 502/504 upstream. latency up across the board.

jake: looking at cloudwatch -> ELB target health shows a lot of targets UNHEALTHY in azc, ENI detach/attach errors in EC2 logs. starting `describe-network-interfaces` audit.

maria: I'm on calls, can someone grab DNS/route53 side? want to know if Route53 is shifting traffic.

tyler: on it. route53 health checks show a slow roll of health check failures toward the us-west-2c endpoints starting ~10:12UTC. but TTLs are low (30s) so we may see gradual bleed to other AZs if failover triggers.

anne: confirmed from control plane logs: API calls to attach ENIs into some instance pools are throttled with `ThrottlingException` in us-west-2c. seeing `eni-attach` error rate spike. EC2 control-plane error 429-ish.

maria: hypothesis: ENI attach/connect storm causing instance agents to fail health checks -> ELB drains -> 5xx. Need mitigation: reduce attach churn, shift traffic away from affected AZ, and protect oncall.

charlie: neteng - can we cross-zone drain targets or force ELB to prefer healthy AZs?

jake: we can temporarily set target group deregistration delay to 0 for affected TGs to speed failover, and enable cross-zone LB balancing if not already. Doing now:
```
aws elbv2 modify-target-group-attributes --target-group-arn arn:aws:... --attributes Key=deregistration_delay.timeout_seconds,Value=0
aws elbv2 set-load-balancer-attributes --load-balancer-arn arn:aws:... --attributes Key=load_balancing.cross_zone.enabled,Value=true
```

infra-bot: Started automation job 7923: draining AZ us-west-2c targets to reduce attachment churn. Job logs: https://ci.redwood.example/jobs/7923

tyler: deploying automation to reduce new ENI attachments: scaling ASG min-size down by 10% for 30m in us-west-2c - this will avoid new instances spinning up and failing to attach.

anne: creating a support ticket with AWS support (SR 1234567891) - control plane throttling reported, asking for temporary quota bump or mitigation guidance.

support-lead: drafting customer-facing update. TL;DR: partial region impact, degraded API performance for a subset of customers routed to us-west-2c. No data loss. Will post status page.

maria: quick checklist for mitigation: 1) Stop churn (tyler scaling) 2) Force ELB to send traffic away (jake modifications) 3) Route53: consider failover policy to use healthy regional endpoints earlier if failures persist 4) Notify customers 5) Oncall rotation signoff.

charlie: Route53 failover: we have weighted records with health checks. If us-west-2c becomes unhealthy, traffic will shift, but TTLs are short so we should get ~30s convergence. We can speed that by temporarily moving weight off affected endpoints using `change-resource-record-sets`.
```
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id ZABCDEFG --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"api.redwood.example.com","Type":"A","SetIdentifier":"us-west-2c","Weight":0,"TTL":30,"ResourceRecords":[{"Value":"3.4.5.6"}]}}]}'
```

jake: applied ELB attrs, started moving weight off us-west-2c targets to 0 for critical records. monitoring.

incident-bot: Update: us-west-2c target count UNHEALTHY -> 68% (was 22% before). 5xx still elevated but trending down slowly.

maria: handing off to tyler for the longer run. I've got to escalate to product for SLA comms. tyler, you're primary now.

tyler: taking over. ETA to stable: 45m-90m depending on AWS SR. continuing automation and watch. tagging postmortem owners: @jake, @maria, @tyler.

support-lead: status.redwood.ai update posted: "Partial degraded performance affecting some requests in us-west-2c; engineers investigating. No data loss. Will update in 30 minutes or sooner." :thumbsup:

anne: AWS responded: control plane is experiencing API throttling for ENI operations in us-west-2c and are performing mitigations. They recommended reducing attach rate and leveraging secondary AZs. AWS asked for list of affected instance IDs, provided.

charlie: we should avoid instance replacements in that AZ for next 2 hours. Also recommend disabling cluster-autoscaler in that region until SR closed. Patching automation to pause scale ups.

infra-bot: Automation note: paused k8s cluster-autoscaler in us-west-2c clusters (clusters: app-prod-1, jobs-prod-1).

tyler: monitoring latency and error rate. Route53 weight change plus ELB cross-zone seems to have shifted ~60% of traffic off the mismatched ENIs. 5xx rate down to ~12% from 40%.

maria: good. collect logs for postmortem: ENI API call rates, ASG events, ELB target health history, Route53 health check history. Put artifacts in the incident folder.

jake: already uploaded pouch: s3://redwood-incident-logs/2234567890/ with ENI traces, ELB logs, and timestamped health check dumps.

support-lead: email to customers sent to affected cohort with mitigation steps and status page link.

tyler: AWS SR updated: they are throttling at control plane and have a mitigation timeline ~2h. They applied internal rate limiting relax to our account, monitoring.

charlie: long-term actions proposed: increase ENI quotas, review attach patterns in our autoscaling policies, add guarded exponential backoff to provisioning workflows, and add synthetic canaries for ENI attach success rate.

maria: agreed. we'll make those action items in the postmortem. For now: keep mitigations until AWS confirms stable for 1h.

incident-bot: Incident state change: Mitigated -> monitoring. P0 -> P1.

tyler: handing back to maria for comms wrap and postmortem. I'll monitor but mark myself as secondary.

maria: thanks all. I'll open postmortem doc and assign owners. link: https://docs.redwood.ai/incidents/2234567890-postmortem (draft).

support-lead: closing note: customer impact window ~10:12 - 11:05 UTC for the worst degradation. We'll include that in the incident timeline. :white_check_mark:
